rows.title: One out of six CT government jobs is vacant as workers keep leaving
rows.standfirst: With nearly 4,000 CT state workers having retired or planning to in the first half of this year, 17% of most Executive Branch jobs are vacant.

rows.title: Businesses, essential workers come up short in final CT budget deal
rows.standfirst: The state budget, which could be adopted Monday, includes no major bailouts for businesses or essential private workers hurt by the pandemic.

rows.title: Money keeps pouring into CT’s coffers; This year’s surplus now $4.8 billion
rows.standfirst: CT legislators awoke to good news Monday as they prepared to debate a new budget: an extra $856 million in tax receipts.

rows.title: CT legislators package unclaimed property reform into budget bill
rows.standfirst: The state treasurer had hoped to return smaller sums to individuals even if they didn’t file a claim, but the new bill would complicate that.

rows.title: House adopts one of the largest tax cuts in CT history
rows.standfirst: The budget positions Connecticut to make an unprecedented $3.5 billion supplemental payment against its massive pension debt.

rows.title: Forecast says CT’s ‘fiscal cliff’ will be gone when pandemic aid expires
rows.standfirst: New projections show state finances will be in the black even after federal pandemic relief is gone in 2025.

rows.title: Analysts: CT could cut taxes $1 billion more within federal rules
rows.standfirst: Senate Minority Leader Kevin Kelly said an estimate from the Office of Fiscal Analysis vindicates the GOP’s calls for bigger tax cuts.

rows.title: Senate adopts ‘humane’ budget that cuts taxes, looks beyond pandemic
rows.standfirst: The Senate voted 24-12, largely along party lines, to adopt the package, which now heads to Gov. Ned Lamont, who is expected to sign it.

rows.title: Lawmakers direct Lamont: Save less, fill vacant state jobs
rows.standfirst: The new CT state budget limits Lamont’s ability to save money once the fiscal year is underway to encourage filling of more vacant state jobs.

rows.title: Did Ned Lamont offer the largest tax cut in CT history? By one standard, yes.
rows.standfirst: Gov. Ned Lamont says his tax relief plan is the largest in CT history, yet it’s a tiny share of the government’s current financial windfall.

rows.title: Ned Lamont to issue $170 million in one-time tax relief this August
rows.standfirst: It is the largest election-year outpouring of one-time relief since Republican Gov. John G. Rowland sought reelection in 1998.

rows.title: CT poised to pay down $3.6 billion in pension debt
rows.standfirst: Regular and supplemental payments into the state’s cash-starved pensions will approach $6.5 billion this year.

rows.title: CT employee unions eyeing arbitration to secure pandemic pay
rows.standfirst: State employee unions say it’s time for government to compensate frontline workers who risked their lives in the pandemic.
